newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai baht weaker late, interbank rate rises.
newsitem.headline: Thai baht weaker late, interbank rate rises.

text.p: The Thai baht eased against the dollar in quiet trade late on Friday but swaps were bullish as Thai banks raised funds to meet their reserve requirement due next Wednesday, traders said.
The baht eased to 26.110-26.113 per dollar late on Friday from 26.105-26.110 in the morning. The one-month baht/dollar swap premium rose to 7.00/7.50 satang/dollar from 6.25/7.25 earlier.
"Some banks, caught a bit short ahead of the reserve deadline, needed to buy swaps," said a Bangkok Bank trader. The market closed on Thursday and will have a holiday on Monday.

"Some players have been selling short for quite some time and now they need to buy it back...even some of the big players are short too," he said. Thai commercial banks must meet reserve requiremnts on the seventh and 22nd of each month.

Swaps were active in the morning partly on market rumours that a planned merger between Thai Danu Bank Plc and Finance One Plc was about to fall apart, dealers said. The bank subsequently denied the rumour.
Demand for funds reduced liquidity and raised the overnight interbank offered rate to 9.75-10.25 percent from 9.50-10.00 quoted in the morning, traders said. -James Mclean (662)652-0642
